extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, reviewers, and readers of observational epidemiology research (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and a 22-item checklist (STROBE) for what should be included when reporting analytical observational studies (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional), intended to improve transparency and completeness of published reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and abstract (Item 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include information about the study's design in the title and abstract; provide an informative and balanced summary of what was done and what was found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the design clear using a commonly used term; the abstract should summarize key methods and results to allow quick assessment by readers and indexers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background/rationale (Item 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the scientific background and rationale for the investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State why the study was done and place it in context of existing knowledge to justify the research question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives (Item 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: State specific objectives, including any prespecified hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about primary and secondary objectives and hypotheses so readers can judge whether analyses address the stated aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design (Item 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present key elements of study design early in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify whether the study is cohort, case-control, or cross-sectional and whether it is prospective or retrospective; this framing should appear early so readers understand the study structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting (Item 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the setting, locations, and relevant dates, including periods of recruitment, exposure, follow-up, and data collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide enough contextual detail (geographic, temporal, clinical) to judge applicability and potential sources of bias related to setting or timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants (Item 6 — design specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Give eligibility criteria, sources and methods of selection of participants; for cohort studies describe follow-up methods; for case-control studies give case ascertainment and control selection and rationale; for cross-sectional, describe selection of participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report numbers invited, examined, included and reasons for non-participation; where appropriate, give matching criteria and numbers in matched studies. Note: item 6 has different versions for cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variables (Item 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly define all outcomes, exposures, predictors, potential confounders, and effect modifiers. Give diagnostic criteria if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise definitions and operationalisation so others can replicate variable measurement and understand what was analysed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sources/measurement (Item 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each variable of interest, give sources of data and details of methods of assessment (measurement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe instruments, procedures, validation, and comparability of assessment methods across groups; where multiple methods exist, explain why a method was chosen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias (Item 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any efforts to address potential sources of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report steps taken to avoid or assess selection bias, information bias, and other systematic errors; be explicit about residual bias that might remain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study size (Item 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the study size was arrived at.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give sample size calculations where applicable or practical considerations that determined size, and discuss implications for precision and power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative variables (Item 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how quantitative variables were handled in the analyses. If applicable, describe which groupings were chosen and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report transformations, categorisations, and reasons for cut-points to allow assessment of potential information loss or arbitrariness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods (Item 12 — design specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe all statistical methods, including those used to control for confounding, examine subgroups and interactions, handle missing data, and account for sampling strategy; specify versions appropriate for study design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State models used, selection of covariates, methods for sensitivity analyses, and software. Item 12 has different expectations depending on cohort, case-control, or cross-sectional design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants — numbers (Results) (Item 13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report numbers of individuals at each stage of study (e.g., numbers potentially eligible, examined for eligibility, confirmed eligible, included in the study, completing follow-up, analysed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider providing a flow diagram; give reasons for non-participation at each stage to help assess selection processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptive data (Item 14 — design specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Give characteristics of study participants (e.g., demographic, clinical, social) and information on exposures and potential confounders, with missing data counts where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide separate information for exposed and unexposed groups or for cases and controls when indicated. Item 14 has versions tailored to different study designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome data (Item 15 — design specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report numbers of outcome events or summary measures over time, with the form appropriate to the study design (e.g., incidence, prevalence, odds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide counts and measures stratified as relevant to cohort, case-control, or cross-sectional designs; item 15 differs across designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main results (Item 16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Give unadjusted and, if applicable, confounder-adjusted estimates and their precision (e.g., 95% confidence intervals). Make clear which confounders were adjusted for and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report category boundaries, translate relative measures into absolute risks where helpful, and present both crude and adjusted results to show effect of confounding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other analyses (Item 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report other analyses done — e.g., subgroup analyses, interactions, and sensitivity analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about which analyses were prespecified vs exploratory and present results with appropriate caution about multiple comparisons or overinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key results (Discussion: Item 18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarise key results with reference to study objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise synthesis that links findings back to the original aims and hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations (Discussion: Item 19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss limitations of the study, taking into account sources of potential bias or imprecision, and both direction and magnitude of any potential bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be candid about weaknesses (e.g., measurement error, residual confounding, selection bias) and their likely effect on conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation (Discussion: Item 20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Give a cautious overall interpretation of results considering objectives, limitations, multiplicity of analyses, results from similar studies, and other relevant evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overstating causal claims when design does not support them; place findings in the context of the totality of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalisability (Discussion: Item 21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the generalisability (external validity) of the study results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider population, setting, and temporal factors that may limit applicability to other groups or contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding (Item 22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Give the source of funding and the role of the funders for the present study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State funder(s) and describe any influence funders had on design, conduct, analysis, or reporting; item 22 may be placed in methods, acknowledgements, or appendix as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design-specific items and separate reporting (asterisked items)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some checklist items (noted by asterisks) require information to be given separately for cases and controls in case-control studies, or for exposed and unexposed groups in cohort and cross-sectional studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure stratified presentation where appropriate so readers can evaluate group-specific characteristics and potential differential measurement or bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE scope and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: STROBE is a checklist intended to provide guidance on how to report observational research well (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional); it is not a prescription for design or conduct, nor is it an instrument to evaluate methodological quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use STROBE to improve transparency and completeness of reporting; use the companion Explanation & Elaboration article for methodological background and examples. Do not treat the checklist as a rigid format — authors may present items in different order or format according to journal style and field traditions.
